bio: Ostend-style shrimp fritters, rabbit stew in stout beer, a German jam doughnut filled with rosemary flavoured crème patissière: such are a few of the culinary gems that explain the success of this tastefully restored former miller’s house in the heart of the unspoiled polder countryside. Ask for a table on the terrace sheltered by panes of glass and admire the landscape. A fan of humble, often overlooked ingredients, the chef has no lack of creativity and his enticing menu appeals to all foodies. The establishment’s continuing popularity is borne out by the lively, bustling vibe that inevitably sets the scene at mealtimes....
